transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Rao (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood PM); Raj, Monica, Evan, Sana (Tideway)

Summary (auto):
Quick product orientation focused on request metadata sanitization, per-route request storage toggles in the Console, and Optimize recommendations for reducing retention costs. Customer has regulatory concerns around PII in shipment manifests and wants to validate that Redwood can run an ephemeral/zero-retention flow for sensitive routes while preserving auditability for others.

Topics covered:
- Console: request storage toggles, per-route retention policies, redaction presets
- API: headers for redaction, request-level ephemeral flag, sampling controls
- Optimize: batching/kv-cache tradeoffs and cost savings estimates
- Security: KMS integration, audit logs, SOC2 questions

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on the Tideway account. We brought Marcus (SE) and Lena (PM). How's everyone doing?
00:06 Raj: Good thanks. Busy week shipping but excited, we got a lot of questions on data handling.
00:10 Marcus: quick intro from me, I focus on infra integrations and perf, I'll be demoing the Console toggles and a couple API examples. Apologies in advance, connection's a little spotty on my side.
00:20 Monica: that's fine. Our key ask: we cannot keep PII for more than 7 days for certain routes, and some manifests must never be stored in plaintext.
00:28 Avery: understood. Today's walkthrough will show three levers: immediate redaction at ingestion, ephemeral request flag for zero-store, and route-level retention policy with sampling for audit logs. We'll also show how Optimize recommends batching that keeps latency within SLOs while cutting token costs.
01:02 Marcus: I'll share my screen — Console > Routes > tideway-shipping-proto.
01:12 (screen share starts, slight audio artifact)
01:20 Marcus: So this is the Routes table. You can see on the right the retention column, right now set to 30 days for the default. If we click into a specific route we have toggles: 'store requests' on/off, 'redact PII' preset drop-down, 'ephemeral' which sets immediate deletion, and 'audit sample rate'.
01:40 Evan: when you toggle ephemeral does that remove the ability to rerun history or retrace issues?
01:46 Marcus: Good question. Ephemeral sets request storage to zero and only records a minimal audit envelope — timestamp, route id, and a non-reversible hash. No user text is stored. You can still get metrics and traces but you lose raw request bodies. If you need retrace, we recommend canarying with sampling at 1% and storing redacted payloads.
02:10 Monica: can we apply the redaction presets on the fly via the API? We have different clients with different PII schemas.
02:18 Marcus: Yes — there's an API header x-redwood-redact: preset=shipping_manifest_v2 or you can pass a JSON redaction schema. We'll demo a cURL.
02:28 Marcus: (demonstrates) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -H 'x-redwood-ephemeral: true' -H 'x-redwood-redact: preset=shipping_manifest_v2' -d '{"input":"...manifest..."}'
02:45 (transcription glitch: some words flattened)
02:50 Raj: that header for ephemeral, x-redwood-ephemeral, is that honored for Dedicated and Private as well?
02:56 Marcus: yes — the runtime honors the header across hosted and dedicated pools. For Private deployments, there is an equivalent config you can gate in your control plane if you want guardrails. There are a few caveats around on-prem storage drivers — we'll link the doc.
03:20 Monica: KMS — can we bring our own key?
03:24 Lena: short answer yes. We support customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest. For hosted we integrate with common cloud KMS (GCP/Azure/AWS). For Private you can point to HSMs or KMS endpoints. All keys are used for request storage encryption; ephemeral mode avoids persistent keys since there is no stored plaintext to encrypt.
03:48 Evan: what's the audit log look like? we need traceability for second-line ops.
03:52 Marcus: The audit log has events for route changes, retention policy updates, and sampled request hashes. It's shipped as a stream to your SIEM or can be stored in Console > Logs with configurable retention. We can deliver via EventBridge or webhooks.
04:10 Sana: procurement question — what's the difference in pricing if we use ephemeral routes for high-volume endpoints?
04:16 Avery: ephemeral reduces storage-based fees dramatically. Compute & tokens still bill as usual. Optimize will show estimated savings if you use batching + ephemeral on high-volume POST endpoints — we can run numbers on your traffic.
04:28 Marcus: (typing) Pulling up Optimize view — here's a sample recommendation: for route 'shipment-ingest', switch to dynamic batching with max latency 120ms; kv-cache TTL of 10s for manifest lookups and set retention to 0 for PII subroute. This change estimates 28% unit cost reduction.
04:52 Raj: latency tradeoff — will batching cause us to miss real-time alerts? we have some SLA alarms on ETA updates.
04:58 Marcus: We can set per-route latency targets. For the critical ETA updates, keep max-batch-size 1 or use a dedicated pool with low-latency SLO. For noncritical ingestion, batching helps cost. You can route critical traffic to Dedicated capacity and cheaper routes to shared hosted.
05:20 Monica: on the redaction presets — are they ML-based or regex? We have nested JSON PII.
05:26 Marcus: presets are a mix: schema-aware redaction (based on supplied JSON path patterns), regex fallback, and ML-based entity detection for free text fields. The ML detection can be tuned to be conservative for compliance. We keep the redaction rules auditable in Console so you can export the rule set.
05:50 Evan: any risk of false redaction — for example, part numbers that look like SSNs?
05:55 Marcus: that happens. We recommend a test dataset run in the sandbox. You can run redaction in 'dry-run' mode where we store both original and redacted (for pilot only) under tighter retention to evaluate false positives.
06:12 Raj: can we enforce SSO and RBAC so only a few users can change retention toggles?
06:16 Avery: yes, Console has RBAC roles. We also support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and audit trails of admin actions. We typically recommend locking retention toggles behind a role and gating via approval workflow if org policy requires it.
06:32 Monica: SOC2 — can you send the SOC2 and pen test results?
06:35 Avery: absolutely, that's in the next steps. I'll attach the compliance pack.
06:40 (marker) Deep-dive API demo
06:42 Marcus: now a short live API run. I'm switching to a sample manifest with sensitive PII. I'll show four calls: baseline (default store), redacted-store, ephemeral, and sample-audit.
06:55 06:55 Marcus: baseline call (no headers) -> response 200, stored. We can see request id r_9f3j2 stored in Console with full payload.
07:15 Marcus: redacted-store call with header 'x-redwood-redact: preset=shipping_manifest_v2,dryrun=false' -> stored redacted payload; original not available via Console. The transcript shows the delete action — note: in our demo environment we use synthetic data.
07:42 Marcus: ephemeral call with x-redwood-ephemeral: true -> request stored only as hash r_h9ab3 with no text. Console shows a blue ephemeral marker and no preview.
08:05 Marcus: sample-audit call with 'x-redwood-sample-audit: 1' will store a copy to the audit buffer; we configure sampling rate by percentage or fixed sampling windows.
08:20 (minor background noise)
08:25 Monica: in the audit copy do you include redacted context or the full payload?
08:29 Marcus: depends on your policy. You can choose to store audited copies as redacted-only. For compliance audits you can store both for a small percentage and route those artifacts to an encrypted S3 in your account.
08:46 Evan: can we run this through our DLP first before it hits Redwood? we have a DLP webhook pipeline.
08:52 Marcus: yes you can chain a pre-ingest DLP that rewrites or tags requests — we honor inbound headers and tags. We also support an integration pattern where the DLP signals redaction schema via a header.
09:10 Raj: about private deployment — if we go Private, do request storage still flow to your Console?
09:15 Lena: for Private deployments you control where request artifacts land. Console may still be used for control plane, but data can be routed to your on-prem storage or cloud bucket in your account; for stricter isolation we can disable any transfer out.
09:30 Monica: procurement — do we need a BAA? we handle PHI at times.
09:35 Avery: we do sign BAA when necessary. That's a common ask for customers with PHI. We'll loop legal on the pilot.
09:44 (small cross talk)
09:50 Marcus: wrap-up demo notes: we'll send sample cURLs, a pilot runbook, and the compliance artifacts. For the pilot we recommend enabling ephemeral on the sensitive route, run 2 weeks of traffic, enable dry-run redaction across a 10% sample, and run Optimize to collect cost estimates.
10:12 Raj: sounds good. On timeline — we'd like to kick off pilot next week if procurement clears.
10:18 Sana: procurement expects redline of Master Services Agreement; we'll need a copy of standard terms.
10:24 Avery: I'll push the contract template and the SOC2 pack. Marcus will provide the technical runbook and sample scripts.
10:33 Evan: one more technical Q — does KV cache TTL interact with redacted payloads? if a cache returns masked values is that safe?
10:39 Marcus: cache keys are derived from hashed request metadata. We avoid caching raw PII unless explicitly enabled. If you enable caching for performance, use policy to store redacted tokens only; Optimize will flag caches that might violate retention policies.
10:55 Raj: ok that addresses most of our compliance concerns.
11:00 Avery: final recap: action items — Avery send compliance docs & contract; Marcus send pilot runbook and cURL examples; Evan confirm SSO and IP allowlist; Tideway to confirm pilot start date. We'll reconvene after docs are reviewed.
11:18 Monica: thank you all. This was useful.
11:22 Avery: thanks everyone, we'll be in touch.

End of transcript.
